questions.question: Which statement best captures the primary goal of large-scale language model pretraining with next-token prediction?
questions.choice_A: Learn general-purpose representations that transfer across tasks and domains
questions.choice_B: Optimize for maximum performance on a single downstream benchmark
questions.choice_C: Memorize as much training data as possible to reduce perplexity
questions.choice_D: Constrain the model to produce only syntactically valid sentences

questions.question: In transfer learning for language models, why can a model pretrained on general web text often perform well after light fine-tuning on a niche domain?
questions.choice_A: Because fine-tuning replaces all model weights with domain-specific parameters
questions.choice_B: Because pretraining discovers reusable linguistic and semantic features that can be adapted
questions.choice_C: Because pretraining guarantees zero-shot exact-match performance on any task
questions.choice_D: Because pretraining eliminates distribution shift effects

questions.question: Compared to training from scratch on a small domain dataset, continual pretraining on that dataset starting from a large general model typically provides what advantage?
questions.choice_A: Lower risk of overfitting because the domain dataset is small
questions.choice_B: Higher perplexity on the domain but improved generalization
questions.choice_C: Better sample efficiency due to strong inductive priors from pretraining
questions.choice_D: No advantage; both approaches converge to the same solution

questions.question: A common failure mode during continual pretraining is catastrophic forgetting. Which description is most accurate?
questions.choice_A: The model’s performance degrades on the new domain due to underfitting
questions.choice_B: The optimizer diverges when the learning rate is too small
questions.choice_C: The tokenizer no longer supports domain-specific vocabulary
questions.choice_D: Performance on previously learned domains decays as the model adapts to the new data

questions.question: Which curriculum strategy is most defensible for stage-wise training when adapting a general LLM to biomedical literature?
questions.choice_A: Pretrain on code first to strengthen reasoning patterns, then continue on biomedical corpora
questions.choice_B: Start directly on biomedical text with a randomly initialized model
questions.choice_C: Begin with instruction tuning, then pretrain on biomedical text
questions.choice_D: Alternate biomedical and multilingual corpora at every step to maximize diversity

questions.question: When mixing data sources during continual pretraining to mitigate forgetting, what is a key design consideration?
questions.choice_A: Always allocate at least 50% of tokens to the new domain to ensure adaptation
questions.choice_B: Adjust mixture ratios based on validation metrics on both old and new domains
questions.choice_C: Exclude high-quality data to prevent overfitting
questions.choice_D: Use uniform sampling across all sources regardless of size or quality

questions.question: Which method conceptually combats catastrophic forgetting by constraining important parameters to remain close to their pretrained values?
questions.choice_A: Gradient accumulation
questions.choice_B: Data deduplication
questions.choice_C: Elastic Weight Consolidation or related quadratic penalties
questions.choice_D: Tokenizer re-training

questions.question: During stage-wise training that begins with code pretraining followed by domain-specific text, what is a plausible risk if the transition is abrupt?
questions.choice_A: The model will permanently disable attention heads used for code
questions.choice_B: The optimizer will automatically reset momentum buffers
questions.choice_C: Loss spikes and regression on code abilities without meaningful domain gains
questions.choice_D: Immediate convergence to a global optimum on both domains

questions.question: Which evaluation protocol best supports early stopping during continual pretraining?
questions.choice_A: Monitor only the training loss on the new domain until it plateaus
questions.choice_B: Track validation perplexity on the new domain and an unchanged holdout from the original mixture
questions.choice_C: Rely exclusively on downstream task scores updated weekly
questions.choice_D: Use parameter count as a proxy for generalization

questions.question: Why might a small learning rate and partial freezing help during initial steps of domain adaptation?
questions.choice_A: They force the model to relearn language from scratch
questions.choice_B: They reduce the variance of stochastic gradients from small domain datasets
questions.choice_C: They prevent any adaptation, preserving generality
questions.choice_D: They encourage rapid specialization via large weight updates

questions.question: What is a practical advantage of using adapters or LoRA-style low-rank updates for continual training?
questions.choice_A: They remove the need for any base model parameters
questions.choice_B: They allow domain specialization with limited catastrophic forgetting by keeping base weights intact
questions.choice_C: They guarantee improvements across all domains without tuning
questions.choice_D: They eliminate the need for data curation in the new domain

questions.question: In the context of data mixing, what does temperature-based sampling aim to achieve?
questions.choice_A: Prioritize the smallest datasets until they are exhausted
questions.choice_B: Linearly scale sampling probabilities with dataset size
questions.choice_C: Reweight source probabilities to balance quality, size, and overexposure risks
questions.choice_D: Ensure deterministic order of samples for reproducibility

questions.question: Which scenario most likely leads to catastrophic forgetting during continual pretraining?
questions.choice_A: Including a small proportion of the original pretraining data in the mixture
questions.choice_B: Using a very small new-domain dataset with aggressive learning rates and no replay
questions.choice_C: Lowering the batch size while keeping the learning rate constant
questions.choice_D: Using mixed precision training for efficiency

questions.question: When deciding between training from scratch versus continual pretraining for a specialized domain with limited compute, which factor is most decisive?
questions.choice_A: Availability of a strong general pretrained model that can be adapted efficiently
questions.choice_B: The number of vocabulary tokens for the new domain
questions.choice_C: The ability to disable positional encodings
questions.choice_D: Whether the domain uses Latin characters

questions.question: What is a common pitfall when evaluating during pretraining to decide on early stopping?
questions.choice_A: Using multiple validation sets
questions.choice_B: Overreliance on downstream task metrics that are noisy or lag behind representation changes
questions.choice_C: Tracking log-perplexity instead of perplexity
questions.choice_D: Maintaining a fixed random seed across runs

questions.question: Why can stage-wise pretraining that starts with code improve subsequent natural language reasoning performance?
questions.choice_A: Code corpora ensure perfect grammar transfer
questions.choice_B: Patterns in code encourage the model to learn precise, stepwise, and long-range dependency structures
questions.choice_C: Code tokens exactly match natural language tokens, improving token embeddings
questions.choice_D: It reduces model size requirements for natural language tasks

questions.question: Which mitigation strategy directly addresses distribution shift during continual pretraining without large architectural changes?
questions.choice_A: Interleaving replay of diverse general-domain data with new-domain batches
questions.choice_B: Switching from Transformers to RNNs mid-training
questions.choice_C: Removing positional encodings to reduce overfitting
questions.choice_D: Shrinking the model width to limit capacity

questions.question: What is a robust approach to checkpoint selection when continual pretraining might trade off old vs. new domain performance?
questions.choice_A: Pick the checkpoint with lowest new-domain validation loss regardless of old-domain metrics
questions.choice_B: Average all checkpoints from the last epoch
questions.choice_C: Select the Pareto-optimal checkpoint balancing old and new domain validation metrics
questions.choice_D: Always choose the earliest checkpoint to minimize overfitting

questions.question: Which practical concern can silently degrade transfer during continual pretraining if not aligned with the new domain?
questions.choice_A: Using gradient clipping
questions.choice_B: Batch size being a power of two
questions.choice_C: Tokenizer coverage and subword segmentation for domain-specific terms
questions.choice_D: The number of attention heads being divisible by 8

questions.question: In large-scale pretraining, what is a sensible stopping heuristic when compute is limited and validation perplexity is still improving slowly?
questions.choice_A: Stop only after reaching zero validation loss
questions.choice_B: Stop when marginal improvements per token of compute fall below a predefined threshold relative to cost
questions.choice_C: Continue indefinitely because more data always helps
questions.choice_D: Stop immediately after any increase in training loss
